rows.l: - For Cell-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the exact cell(s) given in answer_position.
- For Sheet-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the cell range given in answer_position — never touch cells outside that range.
-- Prefer computing and writing LITERAL values (e.g. with pandas/openpyxl) over live spreadsheet formulas, so the result is unambiguous when the file is re-opened for grading.

+- YOUR CODE IS RE-RUN ON HIDDEN INPUTS — so it must COMPUTE the answer, never hardcode it. After you solve the visible file, the grader replays your SAME final code on two other copies of this spreadsheet whose data differs (more or fewer rows, different values) and compares the resulting cell values. Code that only produces the right answer for the visible file scores zero. Therefore:
+  * Never hardcode the answer values, and never type expected results in by hand from the preview or from a worked example. Derive every value from the data actually in the file.

+  * Never copy a demonstration sheet (e.g. a "Wanted Results" / "Desired Results" / sample tab) into the answer — it is illustrative for the visible input only and is wrong for the hidden ones. Reproduce the LOGIC that would generate it.

+  * Detect the real extent of the data programmatically (e.g. the last non-empty row/column). The spreadsheet_content preview shows only the FIRST few rows — never assume the data ends where the preview stops or at a fixed row number, and never restrict a loop to a hardcoded row range.
+  * Use the given spreadsheet_path and output_path strings exactly as provided; do not rebuild them from hardcoded numbers.

+- FORMULAS ARE RE-CALCULATED, BUT SPILL / VOLATILE FUNCTIONS ARE NOT — write those as computed values. The grader recalculates the file with LibreOffice and then compares the resulting cell values. Ordinary scalar formulas (e.g. SUM, SUMIF, COUNTIF, INDEX/MATCH, VLOOKUP, WORKDAY, SUMPRODUCT) recalculate correctly, so you may leave them as formulas OR write their computed value — either works. BUT the following do NOT survive headless recalculation, so compute their result in Python and write the LITERAL value instead:

+  * dynamic-array / spill functions and array constants — TEXTJOIN or WORKDAY over an array like {10,12}, TEXTSPLIT, FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE, and anything openpyxl writes with an `_xlfn.` prefix — recalculate to BLANK or an error;

+  * volatile functions — RANDBETWEEN, RAND, NOW, TODAY — recalculate to different values every run (and cached values read from cells holding them are equally unreliable; recompute from the underlying data).
+  Even when the instruction is phrased as "fix / adjust / write a formula", if the answer needs one of the above, compute what it evaluates to and write the literal result into the cell.

+- MATCH THE EXPECTED DATA TYPE — this matters most for DATES. The grader converts a real date to a number but keeps text as text, then requires the types to match, so a date written as text never equals a real date, and a real date never equals its text form.
+  * If the instruction asks you to CONVERT, PARSE, or STANDARDISE something into a date (or a number), write a REAL datetime / number value — e.g. a real date object, not the string "15/11/2021".
+  * If the instruction asks you to SPLIT, EXTRACT, or COPY a piece of text out of a cell, keep it as the original text string — do not turn it into a datetime.
+  * Write numeric answers as real numbers.
+  * Do not leave a target cell blank because a lookup or match failed, or because a formula branch would return "" — compute the value the instruction calls for, for every row it applies to.
- Always save your result to the exact output_path given, creating any missing parent directories first.
- If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.

2. Solution code that writes the modified file to output_path.
-3. Verification code: re-open output_path and print the values you wrote in answer_position,
-   to confirm they are correct before finishing. If they are wrong, fix your code and write again.
+3. Verification code: re-open output_path (openpyxl, data_only=False) and, for answer_position,
+   print and CHECK each of the following before you finish. If any check fails, fix your code and write again:
+   - The VALUE and Python TYPE of each cell. Confirm the type matches the answer's nature (a real
+     date/number for a converted date/number; text for text you split or copied out). If a cell
+     holds a formula string, it is fine ONLY if it is an ordinary scalar formula (SUM, SUMIF,
+     INDEX/MATCH, VLOOKUP, WORKDAY, SUMPRODUCT, …); if it uses a spill / dynamic-array function
+     (TEXTJOIN/WORKDAY over an array, FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE, `_xlfn.*`) or a volatile
+     function (RANDBETWEEN, NOW, TODAY), it will not recalculate correctly — recompute the value
+     in Python and rewrite.
+   - The COUNT of non-empty cells versus the size of the range. When the instruction fills a
+     column/block, every applicable cell must hold a value; a shortfall means you assumed the
+     data ended too early or a lookup silently failed — fix and rewrite.
+   - That no cell OUTSIDE answer_position was changed.
Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct.
If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
